questions.question: Which tag defines the highest-level heading?
questions.explanation: <h1> is the top-level heading; <h6> is the lowest.

questions.question: Which attribute provides alternative text for accessibility?
questions.explanation: alt describes the image for screen readers and when it fails to load.

questions.question: Which element creates a hyperlink?
questions.explanation: The <a> element with an href attribute creates a hyperlink.

questions.question: Which is the correct HTML5 doctype declaration?
questions.explanation: HTML5 uses the short <!DOCTYPE html> declaration.

questions.question: Which element creates a numbered (ordered) list?
questions.explanation: <ol> creates an ordered list; <ul> is unordered.

questions.question: Which element contains document metadata such as <title>?
questions.explanation: <head> holds metadata like <title>, <meta> and <link>.

questions.question: Which element inserts a line break?
questions.explanation:
creates a line break;
is a thematic break.

questions.question: Which element defines a table row?
questions.explanation: <tr> defines a row; <td> and <th> are cells within it.

questions.question: Which element best represents a self-contained composition such as a blog post?
questions.explanation: <article> represents independent, self-contained content.

questions.question: How is a <label> explicitly associated with an <input>?
options: The label's name matches the input's name
The label's for attribute matches the input's id
The label's id matches the input's for attribute
The label's href points to the input
questions.explanation: The for attribute references the id of the labelable control.

questions.question: Which input type provides built-in email-format validation?
questions.explanation: type="email" validates that the value looks like an email address.

questions.question: If a <form> has no method attribute, which HTTP method does it use?
questions.explanation: The default form method is GET.

questions.question: Which element is inline (not block-level) by default?
questions.explanation: <span> is a generic inline container; the others are block-level.

questions.question: What does the boolean required attribute on an <input> do?
options: Marks the field with a red border only
Blocks form submission while the field is empty
Sends the field even if it is disabled
questions.explanation: required triggers constraint validation that prevents submitting an empty field.

questions.question: Which attribute value opens a link in a new browsing context (tab)?
questions.explanation: target="_blank" opens the link in a new tab or window.

questions.question: What is the purpose of <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">?
options: It sets the page title on mobile
It disables zoom on all devices
It makes the page width match the device width for responsive layout on mobile
questions.explanation: It stops mobile browsers from rendering at a wide virtual viewport and scaling down.

questions.question: What does the defer attribute on an external <script> do?
options: Downloads in parallel and executes after parsing, in document order
Executes as soon as downloaded, in any order
Blocks parsing until the script runs
Delays execution until the user interacts
questions.explanation: Deferred scripts run after the document is parsed, preserving their order; async scripts run when ready.

questions.question: For <div data-user-id="7">, how is the value read in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: data-* attributes appear in dataset with dash-separated names converted to camelCase.

questions.question: What does aria-label on an element provide?
options: A visible tooltip in all browsers
An accessible name for assistive technologies
A CSS hook for styling only
questions.explanation: aria-label defines the accessible name read by screen readers.

questions.question: In , what does the w descriptor indicate?
options: The rendered width in CSS pixels
The intrinsic width of each image file in pixels
questions.explanation: w descriptors tell the browser each candidate's real pixel width so it can choose using sizes.

questions.question: Which of these is a void element (has no closing tag)?
questions.explanation: <input> is a void element; the others require end tags.

questions.question: A <button> inside a <form> with no type attribute behaves as which type?
questions.explanation: The default type of a <button> is submit.
